classification.difficultyReason: Calculate triangle area and an exact hypotenuse from two perpendicular surd lengths.

spec.description: Unshaded right-angled isosceles triangle with vertical left side, horizontal base and descending hypotenuse. Both perpendicular sides are labelled 5\sqrt{3}; the lower-left angle has a square marker. Source blue outlines and grey angle mark are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Both perpendicular sides have length 5\sqrt{3}. No units or hypotenuse length are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the triangle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the length of the hypotenuse.

answer.worked:
By Pythagoras’ theorem, with hypotenuse $h>0$:

$$\begin{align*}h^2&=(5\sqrt{3})^2+(5\sqrt{3})^2\\h^2&=75+75\\h^2&=150\\h&=\sqrt{150}\\h&=5\sqrt{6}\text{ units}\end{align*}$$
